questions.text: Constants $a,b$ satisfy $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\sqrt{ax+b}-2}{x}=1$. Find $a+b$.
questions.explanation: The numerator must vanish at $0$, so $\sqrt{b}=2$ and $b=4$. With the conjugate, the limit is $\frac{a}{\sqrt{b}+2}=\frac{a}{4}=1$, so $a=4$.

questions.text: Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\tan 3x-\sin 3x}{x^3}$.
questions.explanation: $\tan u-\sin u=\tan u\,(1-\cos u)$. With $u=3x$: $\frac{\tan 3x}{x}\cdot\frac{1-\cos 3x}{x^2}\to 3\cdot\frac{9}{2}$.

questions.text: Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 1}\frac{\sqrt[3]{x}-1}{\sqrt{x}-1}$.
questions.explanation: Put $x=t^6$. Then $\frac{t^2-1}{t^3-1}=\frac{t+1}{t^2+t+1}\to\frac23$.

questions.text: Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\frac{\ln(1+3x)}{\sin 2x}$.
questions.explanation: $\frac{\ln(1+3x)}{3x}\cdot\frac{2x}{\sin 2x}\cdot\frac32\to\frac32$.

questions.text: In the unit circle, $P=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$, $Q=(1,0)$ and $R=(\cos\theta,0)$. Let $T(\theta)$ be the area of triangle $PQR$ (blue) and $S(\theta)$ the area between the chord $PQ$ and the arc $PQ$ (red). Find $\displaystyle\lim_{\theta\to 0^+}\frac{T(\theta)}{S(\theta)}$.
questions.explanation: $T=\frac12\sin\theta(1-\cos\theta)\approx\frac{\theta^3}{4}$. $S$ is the sector minus triangle $OPQ$: $S=\frac12(\theta-\sin\theta)\approx\frac{\theta^3}{12}$. The ratio tends to $3$.

questions.text: Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}\frac{\lfloor 3x\rfloor}{x}$, where $\lfloor\cdot\rfloor$ is the greatest integer function.
questions.explanation: $3x-1<\lfloor 3x\rfloor\le 3x$. Divide by $x>0$ and squeeze: both bounds tend to $3$.

questions.text: Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0^+}x\left\lfloor\frac1x\right\rfloor$.
questions.explanation: $\frac1x-1<\lfloor\frac1x\rfloor\le\frac1x$. Multiply by $x>0$: $1-x<x\lfloor\frac1x\rfloor\le 1$, so the limit is $1$.

questions.text: The graph of $f$ stays between the two parabolas: $|f(x)-3|\le(x-1)^2$ for all $x$. Let $h(x)=x^2f(x)$. Find $h'(1)$.
questions.explanation: The bound gives $f(1)=3$, and $\left|\frac{f(1+t)-3}{t}\right|\le|t|\to 0$, so $f'(1)=0$. Then $h'(1)=2\cdot 1\cdot f(1)+1\cdot f'(1)=6$.

questions.text: For the function $f$ in the graph, find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to -1^-}f(x)+\lim_{x\to -1^+}f(x)+\lim_{x\to 1}f(x)+f(1)$.
questions.explanation: Reading the graph: $2+(-1)+1+3=5$. Note that $\lim_{x\to 1}f(x)=1$ even though $f(1)=3$.

questions.text: For the function $f$ in the graph, find $\displaystyle\lim_{t\to 0}f(-1-t^2)+\lim_{t\to 0}f(-1+t^2)$.
questions.explanation: $-1-t^2$ approaches $-1$ from the left, which gives $2$. $-1+t^2$ approaches from the right, which gives $-1$. The sum is $1$.

questions.text: Let $g(x)=\dfrac{3+e^{1/x}}{1+e^{1/x}}$. Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0^+}g(x)-\lim_{x\to 0^-}g(x)$.
questions.explanation: As $x\to 0^+$, $e^{1/x}\to\infty$ and $g\to 1$. As $x\to 0^-$, $e^{1/x}\to 0$ and $g\to 3$. The difference is $-2$.

questions.text: As $x\to\infty$, the graph of $y=\sqrt{4x^2+8x+1}$ has an oblique asymptote $y=mx+c$. Find $m+c$.
questions.explanation: $m=\lim\frac{y}{x}=2$. Then $c=\lim(y-2x)=\lim\frac{8x+1}{y+2x}=\frac{8}{4}=2$.

questions.text: The graph of $y=\dfrac{ax^2+bx+1}{x-1}$ has the oblique asymptote $y=2x+5$. Find $a+b$.
questions.explanation: Long division gives $ax+(a+b)+\frac{a+b+1}{x-1}$. So $a=2$ and $a+b=5$.

questions.text: Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to\infty}x\left(\sqrt{x^2+1}-x\right)$.
questions.explanation: With the conjugate: $\frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2+1}+x}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+1/x^2}+1}\to\frac12$.

questions.text: Let $f(x)=\dfrac{ax^2+bx-6}{x-2}$ for $x\ne 2$ and $f(2)=7$. Find $a^2+b^2$ if $f$ is continuous at $2$.
questions.explanation: The numerator must vanish: $4a+2b=6$. The limit is then the numerator's derivative at $2$: $4a+b=7$. So $a=2$, $b=-1$.

questions.text: Let $f(x)=\dfrac{e^{ax}-1}{x}$ for $x<0$, $\;f(x)=x^2+b$ for $0\le x\le 2$, and $f(x)=\dfrac{x^3-8}{x-2}$ for $x>2$. Find $a+b$ so that $f$ is continuous on $\mathbb{R}$.
Let $f(x)=ax+b$ for $x<1$ and $f(x)=x^2$ for $x\ge 1$. Find $a-b$ if $f$ is differentiable at $x=1$.
questions.explanation: Continuity: $a+b=1$. Equal slopes: $a=2$. So $b=-1$ and $a-b=3$.

questions.text: For the function $f$ in the graph, let $h(x)=(x+1)f(x)$. At how many points of $(-3,5)$ is $h$ discontinuous?
questions.explanation: $f$ breaks at $x=-1,1,4$. At $-1$ the factor $x+1$ sends both sides to $0=h(-1)$, so $h$ is continuous there. At $1$, the limit is $2$ but $h(1)=6$. At $4$, $h$ is unbounded. That leaves $2$ points.

questions.text: Let $g(x)=\dfrac{|x-2|\,(x+3)}{(x-2)(x^2-9)}$. What value at $x=-3$ makes $g$ continuous there?
questions.explanation: For $x<2$, $\frac{|x-2|}{x-2}=-1$, so $g(x)=\frac{-1}{x-3}$ near $-3$. This tends to $\frac16$.

questions.text: Let $g(x)=\dfrac{|x-2|\,(x+3)}{(x-2)(x^2-9)}$. Find $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 2^+}g(x)-\lim_{x\to 2^-}g(x)$.
questions.explanation: After cancelling, $g=\frac{\pm 1}{x-3}$. On the right the sign is $+$, giving $-1$. On the left it is $-$, giving $1$. The jump is $-2$.

questions.text: How many discontinuities does $g(x)=\lfloor x\rfloor\sin(\pi x)$ have on $(0,4)$?
questions.explanation: $\lfloor x\rfloor$ jumps at integers, but $\sin(\pi x)=0$ there, so both one-sided limits equal $g(n)=0$. $g$ is continuous everywhere.

questions.text: How many real solutions does $e^x=3x$ have?
questions.explanation: Let $h(x)=e^x-3x$. Then $h(0)=1>0$, $h(1)=e-3<0$, $h(2)=e^2-6>0$, so there is a root in $(0,1)$ and one in $(1,2)$. $h''>0$, so $h$ is convex and has no more than two.

questions.text: $f$ is continuous on $[0,1]$ with $f(0)=f(1)$. To prove that $f(c)=f\!\left(c+\frac12\right)$ for some $c$ in $\left[0,\frac12\right]$, the Intermediate Value Theorem should be applied to which function on $\left[0,\frac12\right]$?
questions.explanation: $g(0)+g\left(\frac12\right)=f(1)-f(0)=0$, so the two values have opposite signs or are both zero. A zero of $g$ is the required $c$.

questions.text: $f:[0,2]\to[0,2]$ is continuous. Which statement must be true?
questions.explanation: Let $g(x)=f(x)-x$. Then $g(0)\ge 0$ and $g(2)\le 0$, so $g$ has a zero. The constant $f\equiv 2$ rules out the other three.

questions.text: Let $f(x)=x^2|x-3|$. Find the right-hand derivative of $f$ at $3$ minus the left-hand derivative at $3$.
questions.explanation: $\frac{f(3+t)-0}{t}=(3+t)^2\frac{|t|}{t}$. This tends to $9$ from the right and $-9$ from the left, so the difference is $18$ and $f'(3)$ doesn't exist.

questions.text: $f$ is differentiable with $f'(2)=5$. Find $\displaystyle\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{f(2+3h)-f(2-h)}{h}$.
questions.explanation: Split at $f(2)$: $3\cdot\frac{f(2+3h)-f(2)}{3h}+\frac{f(2-h)-f(2)}{-h}\to 3\cdot 5+5=20$.

questions.text: Let $f(x)=x^2\sin\frac1x$ for $x\ne 0$ and $f(0)=0$. Which statement is true?
questions.explanation: From the definition, $\left|\frac{f(h)}{h}\right|\le|h|\to 0$, so $f'(0)=0$. For $x\ne 0$, $f'(x)=2x\sin\frac1x-\cos\frac1x$, which has no limit at $0$.

questions.text: $f$ satisfies $f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y)+2xy$ for all $x,y$, and $f'(0)=3$. Find $f'(2)$.
questions.explanation: Putting $x=y=0$ gives $f(0)=0$. Then $\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}=\frac{f(h)}{h}+2x\to f'(0)+2x$. So $f'(x)=3+2x$.

questions.text: Two tangent lines to $y=x^2$ pass through the point $(1,-3)$. Find the sum of their slopes.
questions.explanation: The tangent at $(t,t^2)$ is $y=2tx-t^2$. Through $(1,-3)$: $t^2-2t-3=0$, so $t=3$ or $t=-1$, with slopes $6$ and $-2$.

questions.text: The tangent to $y=x^3-3x$ at $x=2$ meets the curve again at $x=a$. Find $a$.
questions.explanation: The tangent gives a double root at $2$. The cubic $x^3-3x-(9x-16)$ has no $x^2$ term, so its roots add to $0$: $2+2+a=0$.

questions.text: The curves $y=x^2+ax+b$ and $y=cx-x^2$ share a tangent line at $(1,0)$. Find $abc$.
questions.explanation: From the point: $1+a+b=0$ and $c-1=0$. Equal slopes: $2+a=c-2=-1$. So $a=-3$, $b=2$, $c=1$.

questions.text: The dashed line is tangent to $y=f(x)$ at $x=2$. Let $h(x)=x^2f(x)$. Find $h'(2)$.
questions.explanation: From the graph, $f(2)=3$, and the tangent through $(0,1)$ and $(2,3)$ gives $f'(2)=1$. Then $h'(2)=2\cdot 2\cdot 3+4\cdot 1=16$.

questions.text: Let $p(x)=f(x)g(x)$ for the functions in the graph. Find $p'(1)$.
Let $q(x)=\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}$ for the functions in the graph. Find $q'(5)$.
Let $y=xe^{2x}$. Find $y''(0)$.
For the functions in the graph, let $C(x)=f(g(x))$. Find $C'(5)$.
For the functions in the graph, let $D(x)=g(f(x))$. Find $D'(1)$.
For the functions in the graph, which derivative does not exist?
questions.explanation: $g(2)=2$, which is exactly where $f$ has a corner, and $g'(2)\ne 0$. The composite $f(g(x))$ has a corner at $x=2$.

questions.text: Let $y=\ln(\sec x+\tan x)$. Find $y'\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$.
questions.explanation: $y'=\frac{\sec x\tan x+\sec^2 x}{\sec x+\tan x}=\sec x$, and $\sec\frac{\pi}{3}=2$.

questions.text: The dashed line is tangent to $y=f(x)$ at $x=2$. Let $u(x)=f(x^2-2)$. Find $u'(2)$.
On the curve $x^2+xy+y^2=3$, find the largest $y$-value at a point with a horizontal tangent.
Let $y=x^{\sin x}$ for $x>0$. Find $y'\!\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$.
questions.explanation: $\ln y=\sin x\ln x$, so $\frac{y'}{y}=\cos x\ln x+\frac{\sin x}{x}$. At $\frac{\pi}{2}$: $y=\frac{\pi}{2}$ and $\frac{y'}{y}=\frac{2}{\pi}$.

questions.text: Let $f(x)=x+e^x$ and let $g$ be its inverse. Find $g''(1)$.
On the curve $x^2+xy+y^2=7$, find $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ at the point $(1,2)$.
questions.explanation: $y'=-\frac{2x+y}{x+2y}=-\frac45$. Differentiating $2x+y+(x+2y)y'=0$ again gives $2+2y'+2y'^2+(x+2y)y''=0$, so $5y''=-2+\frac85-\frac{32}{25}=-\frac{42}{25}$ and $y''=-\frac{42}{125}$.

collections.title: Calculus I · Limits (weeks 2–3)
collections.description: Topics: factoring and conjugates; sin x / x and 1 − cos x limits; sandwich theorem with floor functions; one-sided limits from graphs; oblique asymptotes by long division. 14 questions, 50 minutes.

collections.title: Calculus I · Continuity (week 4)
collections.description: Topics: finding parameters at the joins; removable, jump and infinite breaks; sign changes and root counting; fixed points by the IVT. 10 questions, 40 minutes.

collections.title: Calculus I · Derivatives (weeks 5–6)
collections.description: Topics: derivative from the limit definition; tangents from an outside point; product and quotient rules from graphs; chain rule with second derivatives; implicit and logarithmic differentiation. 22 questions, 70 minutes.

collections.title: Calculus I · Practice Quiz 1
collections.description: Topics: limits with tan x − sin x; bounds that give a derivative; continuity with e^(ax) pieces; counting roots of e^x = 3x; chain rule with h''; logarithmic differentiation of x^(sin x). 12 questions, 50 minutes.

collections.title: Calculus I · Practice Quiz 2
collections.description: Topics: limits from a unit circle picture; floor functions and asymptotes; classifying breaks of (x + 1)f(x); functional equations; corners in composite functions; derivatives of inverses. 12 questions, 50 minutes.
